verdict.rationale: Moss documents its own key management: keys can be created, listed, deleted and rotated with overlap through the CLI. It also documents a separate pattern for browser or untrusted clients so the full projectKey is never embedded, which hints at a reduced-privilege credential path. However, the evidence never shows permission scopes, per-index or read-only restrictions, or explicitly agent-scoped tokens. Missing for 10: documented scope/permission model for keys, read-only or per-index restriction, explicit agent-specific least-privilege credential issuance, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can also manage keys from the terminal with the Moss CLI: `moss login`, then `moss keys create`, `list` or `delete`.
Rotate with overlap. Create a new key, move your clients to it, then delete the old one.
Use this pattern from browser or untrusted clients where the `projectKey` must never be embedded in shipped code.
